name: Descriptive Statistics
asig: Descriptive statistics were computed for 4 variables (N = 500). All variables demonstrated skewness values within ±2 and excess kurtosis within ±7 (West et al., 1995; George & Mallery, 2010), indicating approximate univariate normality and suitability for parametric analyses.

name: Correlation Analysis
asig: A Pearson product-moment correlation indicated a statistically significant moderate positive association between "SN1" and "SN2" (r(498) = .46, N = 500, p < .001). This finding suggests that higher values of "SN1" are systematically associated with higher values of "SN2." Note that a statistically significant correlation does not establish causality.

name: Cronbach Alpha
asig: Reliability analysis of the "Subjective Norms (SN)" scale (4 items) yielded Cronbach's Alpha (α) = .69. Although this value falls below the conventional threshold of .70 (Nunnally & Bernstein, 1994), it remains within the acceptable range (.60–.70) for exploratory research (Hair et al., 2019). Scale refinement is recommended before confirmatory use. Examine item-total statistics to identify underperforming items.

name: Independent T-Test
asig: An independent-samples t-test (equal variances assumed) was conducted to compare "SN1" between the Male group (M = 3.45, SD = 0.52) and the Female group (M = 3.47, SD = 0.57). The difference in means (ΔM = 0.02) was not statistically significant at α = .05: t(498) = -0.40, p = .692. Interpret the 95% confidence interval for the mean difference to gauge the range of plausible effects.

name: Paired T-Test
asig: A paired-samples t-test was conducted to evaluate change in "Construct Score" across two related measurement occasions. The mean difference between pre-test (M = 3.46, SD = 0.54) and post-test (M = 3.47, SD = 0.63) (ΔM = 0.01) did not reach statistical significance at α = .05: t(499) = -0.39, p = .698. A 95% CI for the mean difference should be reported to convey the precision of the estimate.

name: One-Way ANOVA
asig: A one-way ANOVA was conducted to examine whether "SN1" differed across levels of "Education." The omnibus F-test was not statistically significant (α = .05): F(3, 496) = 2.41, p = .066. The null hypothesis of equal population group means was retained. Inspect the 95% CIs on group means to evaluate the practical magnitude of any observed differences.

name: Mann-Whitney U
asig: A Mann-Whitney U test was conducted as a non-parametric alternative to the independent-samples t-test, to compare the rank distribution of "SN1" between the Male (Mdn = 3.00) and Female (Mdn = 3.00) groups. The test did not reach statistical significance (α = .05): U = 30587, p = .664.

name: Kruskal-Wallis
asig: A Kruskal-Wallis H test was conducted as a non-parametric omnibus test to compare the rank distributions of "SN1" across levels of "Education." The test did not reach statistical significance (α = .05): H(3) = 7.44, p = .059, indicating no significant difference in rank distributions across groups.

name: Wilcoxon Signed Rank
asig: A Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test was conducted as a non-parametric alternative to the paired-samples t-test, to assess change in "Construct Score" between two related measurement occasions. The test did not reach statistical significance (α = .05): W = 17202, p = .707, with a median difference of 0.00 (pseudo-median of differences).

name: Chi-Square Test
asig: A Pearson chi-square test of independence was conducted to examine the association between "undefined" and "undefined." The test was not statistically significant (α = .05): χ²(117) = 99.50, p = .877. The data are consistent with the assumption of statistical independence between the two categorical variables (Cramér's V = .26, indicating a weak association).

name: Linear Regression
asig: Multiple linear regression was conducted to predict "BEH1" from 2 predictors (α = .05). The overall model was not statistically significant: F(2, N−3) = 0.00, p = 1.000, adjusted R² = .00. The predictors did not explain a significant proportion of variance in "BEH1."

name: Exploratory Factor Analysis
asig: Prior to conducting Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), the suitability of the correlation matrix was evaluated. The Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) measure of sampling adequacy yielded KMO = .72 (middling; Kaiser, 1974). Bartlett's Test of Sphericity was statistically significant (p < .001), confirming that the correlation matrix is sufficiently non-identity for factor analysis. EFA was conducted using Kaiser criterion (eigenvalue > 1; Kaiser, 1974; note: this criterion tends to over-extract), retaining 3 factors with no rotation applied.

name: Confirmatory Factor Analysis
asig: Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) was conducted to evaluate the pre-specified measurement model. The overall pattern of model fit indices indicated excellent fit: CFI = .99, TLI = .98, RMSEA = .02, SRMR = .03 (Hu & Bentler, 1999; Kline, 2016). All reported fit indices satisfy recommended thresholds, supporting the adequacy of the measurement model.

name: PLS-SEM
asig: PLS-SEM measurement model assessment identified violations in the following areas: convergent validity (AVE < .50). These issues must be resolved — by revising items, reconsidering the measurement model, or addressing construct conceptualisation — before the structural model results can be meaningfully interpreted (Hair et al., 2017, 2021). Proceeding with hypothesis testing under measurement model violations risks biased path coefficient estimates and inflated Type I error.

name: Mediation Analysis
asig: Mediation analysis did not support a significant indirect effect of "ATT1" on "BEH1" through "INT1." The Sobel test was not significant (Z = 0.00, p = 1.000). The total effect of "ATT1" on "BEH1" (B = .00, p = 1.000) should be interpreted in the absence of demonstrated mediation.
